editorial:
Imagine stepping back into the chaos of 2002, where the streets of Italy turned into a massive battleground for ideas. You get thrown right into the heart of the G8 summit protests in Genoa, where thousands of people gathered to fight against global power and greed. The vibe is intense and raw, feeling less like a polished movie and more like a first-hand account of a city on edge. You will see the clash between peaceful protesters and the heavy-handed police, making you feel the tension and the anger of the crowd as things spiral out of control.

What really works here is the use of real footage that captures the raw emotion of the time. The pacing is steady, though it can feel a bit heavy since it is a documentary. If you like history or politics, you will find this fascinating, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you are looking for a typical action film. You should definitely try streaming this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best clarity, or maybe rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch. If you love collecting physical media, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is a great way to keep this piece of history.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing the aftermath of the violent clashes in Genoa. You see the long-term damage done to the city and the people who were hurt. It concludes with a look at how these protests failed to change the world immediately but started a huge global conversation about power. The final scenes leave you thinking about whether the struggle was worth it, ending on a serious note about justice and human rights.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves real-life history and social justice stories.
